lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Felipe de Araújo Dias | Lesson 15 -- If I Could Change One Thing

vocab.title: Match each word to its meaning
defs: To give people the authority to make decisions themselves
A small test of a new idea before you use it everywhere
The forms and documents you have to fill in for a process
A disadvantage, or a problem that comes with something good
Agreement and support for an idea from the people involved
To make a process simpler and faster

vocab.text: Notice the pair: a pilot tests the idea, and buy-in gets people behind it. A change with a good pilot and no buy-in still dies in the next meeting.

items: The CEO asks: if you could change one process in your areas tomorrow, what would you change? Say what, why, and what would happen after.
A new store manager asks for advice about a supplier who is always late. Start with if I were you, and give two pieces of advice.
Imagine you had a free year, with no work and no money problems. Where would you live, and what would you do every day?

practice.title: Say each sentence again as an imaginary situation, with the word the cue asks for.
items: We have three approvals, so repairs are slow.
My advice: talk to finance first.
The stores do not have the authority, so they wait.
Maybe we can test it in twenty stores.

items.situation: The CEO asks what you would change first if you had a bigger budget.
tips: If I had a bigger budget, I would...
Say the change, then the result.

items.situation: A colleague asks your advice: should he accept a job in another city?
tips: If I were you, I would...
Give one reason, then one risk.

items.situation: Finance says your idea is not feasible. Defend it in two sentences.
tips: It would cost..., and it would save...
Offer a pilot: we could start with...

items.situation: Someone asks what you would do if you were not in supply chain.
tips: If I were not..., I would...
Add one thing you would miss.

items.situation: Your director asks for the main drawback of your idea.
tips: Be honest: the main drawback would be...
Then say how you would control it.

answerkey.title: Reveal the model answers
list: If we had fewer approvals, repairs would be faster.
If I were you, I would talk to finance first.
If the stores had the authority, they would not wait.
We could test it in twenty stores.
answerkey.note: The second conditional is about a situation that is not real now: if + past, then would, could or might. The past here is not about the past. It is about distance from reality.

listenings.text: Felipe, hi, it's Karen from the CEO's office. A quick message about the directors' offsite next Thursday. This year the format is different. Every director gets five minutes and one question: if you could change one thing in the company, what would it be? Not a plan for the whole year, just one change. Please say what you would change, what would happen if we did it, and what the main drawback would be. If the idea needs money, bring a number. And if I were you, I wouldn't use slides. The CEO prefers people who talk to the room.

Hi Felipe, it's Ingrid. I just wanted to say your talk at the offsite was one of the best. The CEO liked the idea of the store managers approving small repairs, and he wants a pilot. If you started in twenty stores, he would like to see the first results in ninety days. Finance has one condition: a limit for each store, every month. Oh, and one small thing about your English. You said, if I would have the budget. In English, it's if I had the budget. The would only goes in the other half of the sentence. Congratulations again.

extra_audio.text: First, Ingrid asks Felipe what he would change if he could change one thing. Then Felipe says he would cut the three approvals for small repairs. After that, he explains that store managers would solve problems in a day. Next, Ingrid asks about the main drawback. Finally, Felipe says they could start with a pilot in twenty stores.
